environment.docker_vm: Isolated Colima profile, VZ arm64 Linux, 6 vCPU, 8 GiB RAM
environment.api: One Uvicorn worker per run; separate API images for current and stored size, both with fixed prefetch 8, adaptive off, and the 2 MiB hard limit on.
environment.client: One host Python 3.13.14 process per run; SDK uses the checked-out source
environment.fixture_database: Both profiles in one PostgreSQL database and in separate uploads.

fixture.fixture: Identical Base64(SHAKE-256(width, width ordinal)) payloads in two orders

current.description: Untimed verification of NDJSON payload bytes in actual returned PostgreSQL batches. The byte cap excludes PostgreSQL wire framing, SQL work memory and process RSS.

stored.description: Untimed verification of NDJSON payload bytes in actual returned PostgreSQL batches. The byte cap excludes PostgreSQL wire framing, SQL work memory and process RSS.

method.execution: Fresh PostgreSQL and API containers per run, persistent fixture volume; no manual host/VM page-cache drop. SDK validates ordering, row count, wire bytes and SHA-256 for each export.
method.cpu: API and PostgreSQL cgroup cpu.stat deltas around SDK invocation; client process CPU during concurrent export. Average cores divide CPU seconds by wall time reported by SDK.
method.memory: Kernel cgroup lifetime memory.peak for both fresh containers (includes startup, page cache and other cgroup memory); PID 1 VmHWM for API and ru_maxrss for SDK. PostgreSQL query-process RssAnon is a sampled sum of simultaneous observations, plus largest individually observed backend VmHWM. Non-idle includes idle-in-transaction backends with an open export.
method.current_hard: One ordered index scan through a lazy materialized window. PostgreSQL serializes JSONB when reading to determine the complete UTF-8 NDJSON row size including the envelope and LF; the API assembles the unchanged envelope. The 2 MiB cap excludes protocol framing, PostgreSQL work memory and process RSS.
method.stored_hard: A trigger records the UTF-8 byte size of JSONB on write. The hard-limit query uses the stored size for its ordered budget window, and serializes payloads selected for export. Both images query the same fixture volume with the extra column and trigger; the current image ignores the stored size.
method.alternating: A 220-byte JSONB payload before every wide payload.
method.bursts: 65 narrow then 64 wide; 62 groups of 64 narrow then 64 wide; 63 narrow then 64 wide.
method.wide_rows: First of every four wide payloads is 768 KiB; the other three are 256 KiB. Both profiles use the same counts and total bytes.
method.comparison: Warmups excluded; summary contains per-run min, median and max for each profile, concurrency and prefetch mode.

stored_size_verification.serialization_placement_verified: The convert_to Result node executes once for each returned row after LIMIT, in both custom and generic plans.
stored_size_verification.schema_upgrade_check: Idempotent init, unchanged heap file, fallback for old rows, UTF-8 length on LATIN1, replica updates and partitions verified separately.

supplemental_binary_copy_overhead.method: Separate database, same schema and FK receipt. One warmed server-side binary COPY file for both modes. Start psql, COPY and durable COMMIT timed inside the container; trigger toggle, TRUNCATE, CHECKPOINT and verification are outside timing. PostgreSQL cgroup CPU includes the local psql process. HTTP, application validation and receipt writes are not measured.
